pharm: Peripherally acting antitussive that reduces activity of sensory C-fibre cough receptors in the airways, lowering the afferent input that triggers the cough reflex without central depression.

May be taken on an empty stomach; not affected significantly by food
Contraindicated in severe impairment; caution otherwise
Avoid; possible additive drowsiness in sensitive individuals
Cough response; drowsiness and ability to drive; hypersensitivity reactions
summary: Levodropropizine is a peripherally acting, non-opioid antitussive used for symptomatic relief of dry, non-productive cough. It acts on airway sensory C-fibre receptors to dampen the cough reflex without depressing the central nervous system or respiration. The usual adult dose is 60 mg (10 mL of 6 mg/mL syrup, or one tablet/sachet) up to three times daily with at least 6 hours between doses, and treatment is generally limited to about 7 days. Although largely non-sedating, some drowsiness can occur, so caution is advised with driving and alcohol. It is contraindicated in bronchorrhoea/reduced mucociliary clearance, severe hepatic impairment, and pregnancy/lactation. It is not FDA-approved and is marketed in Europe and parts of Asia (Italy, India, Korea); dosing is from the SmPC/manufacturer label and BNF.

moa: Levodropropizine is the levo-enantiomer of dropropizine and acts predominantly at the peripheral level. It modulates the activity of sensory neuropeptide-containing C-fibres in the tracheobronchial tree, reducing the sensitivity of airway cough receptors and the afferent neural input that generates the cough reflex. It also shows some anti-inflammatory and antihistamine-like (mast-cell stabilising) activity. Because it does not act on the cough centre in the central nervous system, it produces little sedation or respiratory depression and does not impair mucociliary clearance, distinguishing it from opioid (central) antitussives.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to levodropropizine or any excipient
Bronchorrhoea and conditions with marked bronchial hypersecretion
Reduced mucociliary clearance (e.g. Kartagener's syndrome, primary ciliary dyskinesia)
relative: Patients in whom drowsiness would be hazardous (driving, operating machinery)
monitor: Cough character (switch to productive cough warrants reassessment)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Animal studies have shown reproductive toxicity and there are inadequate human data, so it must not be used during pregnancy.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. Levodropropizine is excreted in animal milk; because of the potential risk to the infant, do not use while breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance below 35 mL/min), as the drug and its metabolites are eliminated renally. No specific dose reduction is established in the label, but careful use and monitoring are advised.
hepatic: Contraindicated in severe hepatic impairment. Use with caution in mild to moderate hepatic impairment.

moderate: CNS depressants / sedatives (e.g. benzodiazepines) - possible additive central depressant effect in sensitive individuals; caution
minor: No clinically significant effect on oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin) or on insulin/oral antidiabetic activity reported in studies
interactions.food: Absorption is not markedly affected by food; may be taken on an empty stomach.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it may add to any drowsiness in susceptible patients.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically important interference with routine laboratory tests reported.

monitoring: Response of the cough and whether it becomes productive
Daytime drowsiness and fitness to drive or operate machinery
Liver function if symptoms suggest hepatic involvement
counsel: Take doses at least 6 hours apart and do not take more than the recommended daily amount
Use only for a dry, tickly cough and stop if the cough becomes productive (phlegmy) or lasts more than about a week
This medicine may occasionally make you drowsy - be careful when driving or using machinery until you know how it affects you
Seek urgent help if you develop a rash, facial or throat swelling, or difficulty breathing
pk: Rapidly absorbed after oral dosing; antitussive effect within about 1-2 hours
Plasma Tmax about 0.25-2 hours (rapid absorption, bioavailability >75%)
Several hours per dose; dosed up to three times daily at least 6 hours apart
Store below 25 C in the original packaging, protected from light
pearls: Not FDA-approved; dosing here is taken from the SmPC (Italian/Korean Levopront/Levotuss labels), manufacturer label, and BNF where available
Peripheral mechanism means little sedation, dependence, or respiratory depression compared with opioid (central) antitussives, and it does not reduce mucociliary clearance
Reserve for dry, non-productive cough - contraindicated when there is excess bronchial secretion (bronchorrhoea) or impaired ciliary clearance
Some drowsiness can still occur, so counsel about driving and avoid alcohol or other CNS depressants
Limit treatment to about 7 days and reassess; contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, and children under 2 years
missed: If you miss a dose, take it when you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose; keep at least 6 hours between doses and never take two doses together. As it is used as needed for cough, a missed dose can simply be skipped.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; no significant effects were seen with single doses up to 240 mg or 120 mg three times daily for several days. A transient, mild tachycardia may occur. There is no specific antidote; manage with symptomatic and supportive care, and seek medical attention or contact a poisons centre for significant ingestions.
